A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, algorithms, and complete appendices are readable, allowing revisions to be distinguished from relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical regret guarantees, and proofs, including its bandit-game application. Neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its additional universal-regret guarantee is supported by mathematical analysis, with no experiments, simulations, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds a separate worst-case universal ensemble combining Adapt-ML-Prod, bandit gradient descent, and a shared spherical two-point estimator. Retained procedures also change: Algorithm 1 uses shrinkage δ/r instead of δ/R, Table 2 changes the strongly convex step size from 2/(λ_i t) to 4/(λ_i t), and Eq. (E.7) restores a squared prediction-error term.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirically evaluated tasks. The removed game application and added universal-regret extension are theoretical analyses.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Table 1 retains the same analytical comparison with Chiang et al. (2013).

E3.justification: Neither PDF contains an empirical evaluation protocol. Revised algorithm parameters and theoretical assumptions do not represent changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical robustness or sensitivity tests, error analyses, or experimental case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changes to concentration bounds and estimator moments concern mathematical proofs.

E6.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental numerical or qualitative outcomes. Table 1's analytical bound entries are unchanged; revised theoretical guarantees and proof constants are covered under T1.

T1.justification: Appendices A, C, D, and E substantially revise estimator bounds, sampling-gap arguments, and regret proofs. For example, the maximal expected squared estimator-optimism difference changes from 4dG² to 8dG² plus the retained remainder, and new Lemma 21 supplies a conditional-moment argument for universal regret. New Theorem 11 establishes worst-case universal bounds without smoothness, while v1's game Theorems 8 and 12 are removed. Obliviousness is made explicit, and the dynamic-regret definition now averages both queried losses.

C1.justification: The principal dimension-dependent guarantees remain, but v2 removes the advertised fast-convergence contribution for bandit games from the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It explicitly restricts environments and dynamic comparators to oblivious choices and adds a claim of first worst-case universal regret bounds in Section 5.2.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability qualifications: adaptive environments remain unresolved, exp-concave losses pose additional difficulties, and the dynamic-regret guarantee retains an extra dimension factor relative to the worst-case benchmark. Remark 3 also explains how storing the latest coordinate-sign observation serves gradient variation differently from reservoir-based gradient-variance estimation.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly specifies the number of dynamic-regret base learners, and explicit parameter recipes are revised, including the exploration radius for the nonsmooth algorithm in Appendix C.5. The practical binary-search construction already existed in v1; neither version provides code, hardware, or execution information.

R1.justification: v2 expands contextual citations, including Motwani and Raghavan (1995), Gaillard et al. (2014), and additional dynamic and universal online-learning work. It sharpens the comparison with the Hazan–Kale estimator, while retaining the central positioning against Chiang et al. (2013).

P1.justification: Sections 3.1 and 5 receive substantial explanatory rewriting, with guided derivations and fuller descriptions of the ensemble frameworks. Section 5 becomes two named subsections instead of three brief application items. Existing coupon-collector and Bregman-divergence material is brought forward from the appendices, alongside widespread language editing.

P2.justification: The two tables and six numbered algorithm boxes retain their basic designs, and neither version contains figures. v2 reformats Theorem 7 into a displayed case distinction, shifts algorithm boxes relative to nearby prose, and updates the publication footer, producing limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important mathematical deficiencies: Algorithm 1 corrects feasible-domain shrinkage, Appendix A repairs moment and bias calculations, and Appendix E.2 strengthens the strongly convex universal-regret proof through new Lemma 21. Explicit obliviousness restrictions make applicability clearer. Although the game contribution is withdrawn and some bounds become more conservative, the improvements to feasibility, proof support, and claim precision provide a substantial net gain in rigor.
